name.text: Predicting school arrival times using weather-dependent tree diagrams

questiontext.text:
The probability that it rains on a school day in Nairobi is {@str_R@}. If it rains, the probability that Atieno arrives late for school is {@str_LR@}. If it does not rain, the probability she is late is {@str_LNR@}.

Draw a two-stage tree diagram for this scenario and use it to solve the following questions:

a) Find the probability that Atieno is late for school.

(Enter your answer as an exact decimal).

\(P =\) [[input:ans1]]

[[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

b) Find the probability that it rained, but she was NOT late.

\(P =\) [[input:ans2]]

[[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution:

First, establish the probabilities for all branches on the tree diagram:

  • \(P(\text{Rain}) = {@str_R@}\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(P(\text{No Rain}) = 1 - {@str_R@} = {@str_NR@}\)
  • \(P(\text{Late} \mid \text{Rain}) = {@str_LR@}\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(P(\text{Not Late} \mid \text{Rain}) = 1 - {@str_LR@} = {@str_LNR_given_R@}\)
  • \(P(\text{Late} \mid \text{No Rain}) = {@str_LNR@}\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(P(\text{Not Late} \mid \text{No Rain}) = 1 - {@str_LNR@} = {@str_NL_given_NR@}\)

Part a: Probability she is Late
The event "Atieno is late" corresponds to two paths on the tree diagram: (Rain \(\rightarrow\) Late) and (No Rain \(\rightarrow\) Late).

\( \displaystyle P(\text{Rain, Late}) = {@str_R@} \times {@str_LR@} = {@path_R_L@} \)

\( \displaystyle P(\text{No Rain, Late}) = {@str_NR@} \times {@str_LNR@} = {@path_NR_L@} \)

Add these path probabilities together:

\( \displaystyle P(\text{Late}) = {@path_R_L@} + {@path_NR_L@} \)

\( \displaystyle \boxed{ P(\text{Late}) = {@ta1_str@} } \)

Part b: Rain and Not Late
This corresponds to a single path on the tree diagram: (Rain \(\rightarrow\) Not Late).

\( \displaystyle P(\text{Rain, Not Late}) = P(\text{Rain}) \times P(\text{Not Late} \mid \text{Rain}) \)

\( \displaystyle P(\text{Rain, Not Late}) = {@str_R@} \times {@str_LNR_given_R@} \)

\( \displaystyle \boxed{ P(\text{Rain, Not Late}) = {@ta2_str@} } \)

The tree diagram:

[[jsxgraph width="460px" height="182px"]] (function() { var L1 = [['Rain', '{#float(P_R)#}'],['No rain', '{#float(P_NR)#}']], L2 = [[['Late', '{#float(P_LR)#}'],['Not late', '{#float(P_LNR_given_R)#}']],[['Late', '{#float(P_LNR)#}'],['Not late', '{#float(P_NL_given_NR)#}']]], LV = ['{#path_R_L#}','{#float(P_R*P_LNR_given_R)#}','{#path_NR_L#}','{#float(P_NR*P_NL_given_NR)#}']; var n = 4, wide = LV.length ? 15 : 12; var b = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, {boundingbox:[-0.4, n + 0.4, wide, 0.3], axis:false, grid:false, showNavigation:false, showCopyright:false, pan:{enabled:false}, zoom:{enabled:false}}); function lab(p, q, t, txt) { // t: how far along the branch the label sits // probability label 55% along the branch, above an upward branch and below a downward one var x = p[0] + t*(q[0]-p[0]), y = p[1] + t*(q[1]-p[1]); var off = (q[1] >= p[1]) ? 0.32 : -0.32; b.create('text', [x, y + off, txt], {anchorX:'middle', anchorY:'middle', fontSize:13, fixed:true, strokeColor:'#1565c0'}); } var y = n, k = 0, root = [0, (n + 1)/2]; b.create('point', root, {name:'', size:3, fixed:true, color:'#333', showInfobox:false}); for (var i = 0; i < L1.length; i++) { var m = L2[i].length, ymid = y - (m - 1)/2, p1 = [3.0, ymid]; b.create('segment', [root, p1], {strokeColor:'#555', fixed:true}); lab(root, p1, 0.55, L1[i][1]); b.create('text', [3.15, ymid, L1[i][0]], {anchorY:'middle', fontSize:15, fixed:true}); for (var j = 0; j < m; j++) { var s2 = [6.3, ymid], p2 = [9.2, y]; b.create('segment', [s2, p2], {strokeColor:'#555', fixed:true}); lab(s2, p2, 0.72, L2[i][j][1]); b.create('text', [9.35, y, L2[i][j][0]], {anchorY:'middle', fontSize:15, fixed:true}); if (LV.length) b.create('text', [12.0, y, LV[k]], {anchorY:'middle', fontSize:13, fixed:true, strokeColor:'#2e7d32'}); y -= 1; k++; } } })(); [[/jsxgraph]]

questiondescription.text:
This question is based on the tree-diagram examples (second stage depends on the first) in the section Tree Diagrams of the CBC Grade 11 Mathematics textbook (INNODEMS).

Tree Diagrams: Conditional Probability Paths

truefeedback.text: Correct. You accurately identified both paths that lead to being late and added their probabilities.

node.description: Check if they only calculated the Rain -> Late path

truefeedback.text: You calculated the probability that it rains AND she is late. However, she can also be late on a day with no rain. You must calculate both paths and add them together.

falsefeedback.text: Incorrect. Calculate \(P(\text{Rain}) \times P(\text{Late} \mid \text{Rain})\), then calculate \(P(\text{No Rain}) \times P(\text{Late} \mid \text{No Rain})\), and add the two results.

truefeedback.text: Excellent. You correctly multiplied the probability of rain by the conditional probability of not being late given rain.

falsefeedback.text: Incorrect. Multiply the probability of rain by the probability of not being late given that it rained (\(1 - {@str_LR@}\)).
